name: Trusty
label: Dischord
lede: A pop-punk band from Little Rock that loved DC so much they moved there, earned a spot on Dischord, and wrote a song named after the Orange Line.

eras.title: Little Rock's own
eras.text: Before they were a Dischord band, Trusty were one of Little Rock's best-known underground groups. By 1990, Dischord notes, they had already put out records and toured the country, all from Arkansas.

years.p: [[Bobby Matthews|0cec47d8-1869-44fe-b493-f79256499cc3]] and [[James Brady|d0d20648-e57e-46b4-9d1f-28fc9ce0a2d7]] on guitars and vocals, Paul Bowling on bass, Bircho Birch on drums. The Arkansas Democrat-Gazette credits Matthews with founding Trusty.
years.xp: AllMusic lists Trusty's first line-up as Brady, Matthews, "Paul" and "Bircho"; Wikipedia gives their surnames as Bowling and Birch. Punk in Little Rock was a small world, and Trusty quickly became one of its best-known bands.

years.h: Trusty's first EP, A Name to Depend On
years.p: Trusty's first proper release comes out on Soma Records.
Trusty's debut full-length comes out on Truant Records. By now, per Dischord, the band had toured the country too.

years.h: Bassist Paul Bowling out, Brad Long in
years.p: Paul Bowling leaves Trusty. [[Brad Long|107b528c-35a8-493d-9f83-df90a95210b2]], formerly of Sobering Consequences, takes over on bass, per AllMusic.

eras.title: Fans move to the capital
eras.text: Dischord puts it simply: several Trusty members were devoted fans of the DC scene and moved there in 1992. Wikipedia describes the next few years as a long campaign to earn respect from a local scene that did not hand it out to newcomers.

years.h: Trusty move from Little Rock to Washington
years.p: Trusty relocate to DC. Wikipedia says 1992 to 1996 was spent working to gain respect and recognition from the established DC punk scene.
years.xp: Dischord's own history frames the move as fandom: several Trusty members were devoted to DC's music and moved to be part of it. They arrived with records and national tours already behind them, which in DC counted for less than showing up.

years.p: Trusty's first release after moving to DC, on Sidekick Records.

years.h: Drummer Bircho Birch out, Jim Schaffer in
years.p: AllMusic places Trusty's drum change after Cockatoo. [[Jim Schaffer|b1513e4a-6075-45f0-b86e-9b62ac9ad321]] completes the line-up that made both Dischord records.
The Arkansas Democrat-Gazette dates Trusty's Dischord signing to 1994. Truant also issues The Paul Years Retrospective that year, collecting the first line-up with Paul Bowling.

eras.title: Two Dischord records and out
eras.text: Trusty got two albums on Dischord, the label they had moved across the country for, Goodbye Dr. Fate and The Fourth Wise Man, and took them to Europe. Then, in the summer of 1997, with another US tour ahead, they quit and headed back south.

years.h: Goodbye Dr. Fate, a year in the making · Dischord No. 93
years.p: Trusty produced their first Dischord album themselves between November 1993 and October 1994 at WGNS and Inner Ear. Fourteen songs of hooky, bright punk.
years.xp: The title nods to the DC Comics sorcerer Doctor Fate, and there's a song called "Kal-el" too. Session dates are from Wikipedia; the studios from Dischord.

years.p: Trusty's second Dischord album, recorded at Inner Ear. Twelve songs, closing with "Orange Line", named for the DC Metro line, by a band that now lived on it. Also: "A Shit-Ass Scene For Nature Boy."

years.h: Trusty tour Europe for the first time
years.p: AllMusic says Trusty toured Europe for the first time in 1996, the year The Fourth Wise Man came out. Dischord says they covered North America and Europe.

years.cap: The four who made the Dischord records
years.h: Trusty quit on the eve of a US tour
years.p: AllMusic says Trusty announced the breakup in July 1997, right before what would have been their third major US tour. Dischord dates the end to summer 1997, as members moved south.
years.xp: Other sources run later: Wikipedia and the Arkansas Democrat-Gazette both say Trusty folded in 1998, which may reflect when the last of it wound down. Dischord's summer 1997 is used here.

eras.title: Reunions, outtakes and an art class
eras.text: Trusty never quite stayed gone. There were new bands, a string of reunions, the outtakes record Sugar Smack on a Little Rock label, and a formal end in 2008.

years.h: James Brady and Jim Schaffer form the Blisters
years.p: Trusty's James Brady and Jim Schaffer form the Blisters with Kathy Cashel of [[Norman Mayer Group|4178dab8-59f4-4c04-8b99-de46a160eb87]], per AllMusic. Wikipedia lists a Trusty reunion that year too.
Trusty's song "Goodbye Dr. Fate" lands on Dischord's anniversary box set, Dischord No. 125.
Max Recordings, a Little Rock label, releases a collection of Trusty outtakes. The Arkansas Times reported the band reuniting in late 2005.

years.h: Trusty's 1987 demo reissued; the band officially ends
years.p: Trusty reunited again, and DC-Jam Records reissued their 1987 demo, recorded two years before the band's official start. AllMusic marks 2008 as the formal end.

years.h: Bobby Matthews, art teacher and improviser
years.p: The Democrat-Gazette reports Trusty founder Bobby Matthews taught elementary-school art in Memphis for 15 years, and that a comedy bit at a Trusty reunion show pushed him into improv. By 2016 he co-ran a Little Rock comedy show.

sources.title: Arkansas Democrat-Gazette: Ex-punk rocker, theater director form momandpop show
